      <description><p>Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded</p><p>Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.</p><p>Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state">Continue reading...</a></description>

A father and daughter detained by masked ICE officers on an airport jet bridge in Seattle has sparked a renewed outcry over the Trump administration’s immigration policies, with the governor of Washington state calling US federal immigration agents "out of control". Other passengers boarding the Alaska Airlines flight at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport on Saturday used their cellphones to film the father and daughter being detained by the officers, who were wearing unmarked jackets and khaki pants. The recordings were widely viewed on social media.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ba1e9d0a-e727-11f1-bc39-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261123-102228-102416-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ba1e9d0a-e727-11f1-bc39-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261123-102228-102416-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">bf46ae1c-e727-11f1-9360-03fe648965b3</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:34:43 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>The worst COP ever? Climate talks collapse in chaos</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261123-the-worst-cop-ever-climate-talks-collapse-in-chaos</link><description>
The COP31 climate talks ended in failure Sunday as a contentious deal collapsed over fossil fuels and the summit in Turkey stretched into record overtime. The final agreement was rejected in a chaotic finale to a UN climate summit that ran two days over schedule, underscoring the strains on diplomacy in an increasingly fractured world. <![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:00:00 +0000 en <![CDATA[ Astronomers just discovered a rare triple star system 28 light-years away, and they have ‘no clean explanation for how it got here’ ]]> A triple system containing a dim red dwarf star and not one but two white dwarfs has been fortuitously discovered just 28 light-years away from our solar system.

"We were actually looking for planets," Étienne Artigau of the Trottier Institute for Research on Exoplanets at the Université de Montréal, who led the discovery, said in a statement. "Instead, we found something much more surprising."

So surprising that there are no similar systems within at least 100 light-years. Furthermore, the configuration of the system seems impossible. "This system should not exist," added Montreal's Patrick Dufour. "We have no clean explanation for how it got here."

This triple system has been called Welopō'ai, which is a portmanteau of two Hawaiian words that means a 'path of family traits', and to understand the mystery behind it requires astronomers to figure out the history of the three objects.

A white dwarf is what remains when a star of similar mass to our sun reaches the end of its life. As it begins to run low on hydrogen for nuclear fusion reactions in its core, the star's energy generation begins to falter and its interior starts to contract under gravity. This has the effect of raising the temperature throughout the star, causing an outer shell of hydrogen to ignite its own fusion reactions. The star promptly bloats to become a red giant tens or even hundreds of millions of kilometers across.

Soon enough the star ceases fusion reactions completely. The star's outer layers are shed and they expand out into space, while its core contracts to become an inert white dwarf with a diameter similar to Earth but with a mass generally between half and two-thirds of a solar mass.

Therefore, the Welopō'ai system was once a triple system with two sun-like stars plus the red dwarf. Now the two sun-like stars have undergone this stage of star death while their companion red dwarf continues to linger, since its low mass bequeaths it a longer life because it does not use up its core hydrogen as quickly.

One of the white dwarfs orbits the red dwarf at a distance of 129.3 astronomical units (19.3 billion kilometers or 12 billion miles) and takes about 1,000 years to complete one orbit. This white dwarf and the red dwarf were previously known, and Artigau's team had been using the SPectropolarimètre InfraROUge (SPIRou) instrument on the Canada–France–Hawaii Telescope atop Mauna Kea to search for planets orbiting the red dwarf when they noticed something highly unusual.

SPIRou discovers planets by measuring how much their gravity tugs on their host star. Think of a star and planet orbiting a kind of gravitational balancing point between them called a center of mass. This center of mass is usually inside the star, since the star is far more massive than the planet, but crucially not at its very center, so the star appears to wobble to and fro around the combined center of mass.

The spectrometer measures this wobble in the form of a Doppler shift in the star's light that can be translated into the velocity at which the star is moving around this center of mass. Astronomers call this a 'radial velocity'. A large gas giant like Jupiter might incur a radial velocity of hundreds of meters per second, while an Earth-mass planet generates a radial velocity of tens of meters.

Yet the object that SPIRou found orbiting close to the red dwarf was creating a huge radial velocity signals of 10 miles (16 kilometers) per second. Whatever it was, it was not a planet. With the help of the eight-meter Gemini North telescope on Hawaii's Mauna Kea, Artigau's team were able to identify the mystery object as a white dwarf.

"The unusual combination of high mass and very low brightness left only one plausible explanation: it was the remnant of a dead star," said Charles-Antoine Parent, an undergraduate student at Université Laval and a co-author of the study.

White dwarfs are not exactly rare, and even finding two white dwarfs together is not unheard of: WD 0727+482 is a binary white dwarf system 37 light-years away, for example. To encounter two white dwarfs in a triple system with a regular star though is a precious find.

The reason being that the masses of white dwarfs are not generally well defined. Yet their masses are not random; they are directly connected to the mass of the star that produced them.

Thanks to the newly discovered white dwarf being separated from the red dwarf by about 4.6 astronomical units (688 million kilometers/428 million miles) – that's closer than Jupiter orbits our sun – Artigau's team were able to measure their masses to within an uncertainty of less than 1%. They found that the red dwarf has a mass 42% that of our sun and the newly discovered white dwarf has a mass 62% that of our sun. When the white dwarf was a regular star it would have had a mass 40% greater than our sun. The second more distant white dwarf orbits the pair of them.

The Welopō'ai system is therefore a good system for testing our models of stellar evolution that dictate how massive a white dwarf should be. If we know the white dwarf's mass with high precision, scientists can also use that as a starting point from which to explore the extreme physics of the white dwarf's condensed matter, which is being held up and prevented from contracting any further by something called electron degeneracy pressure – the unwillingness of negatively charged electrons to crush down any further and merge with positively charged protons to form neutrons. That takes the extra gravity from a more massive star to form a neutron star.

So why should Welopō'ai not exist? The trouble is that when stars turn into red giants they really stir things up. Even if the red giant didn't expand out as far as the red dwarf, the expansion should have destabilized the red dwarf's orbit and potentially even caused it to crash into the red giant. Yet here the red dwarf is in a happily stable orbit like nothing had happened.

"That is the question driving our next observations," said Dufour. It is hoped that further, more detailed, measurements of the gravitational interactions between the three members of the Welopō'ai system will help the team disentangle the evolutionary history of the trio to better understand their orbits and how the red dwarf survived. And because they are so relatively close to us, we have the advantage of being able to make high-precision measurements.

"Discoveries like this remind us that our own cosmic neighborhood still contains remarkable surprises," said Artigau. "Even when we're searching for planets, our universe often has something completely unexpected waiting for us."

The discovery of the Welopō'ai triple system is described in a paper published on Nov. 19 in Astronomy & Astrophysics.

]]> <![CDATA[ SpaceX launches 2 rockets from same pad 32 hours apart, smashing turnaround record (video) ]]>

SpaceX set a new record with its latest satellite launch out of California.

A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base's Launch Complex-4E on Sunday (Nov. 22) at 7:23 a.m. ET (1223 GMT; 4:23 a.m. local time in California), on a mission for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) called NROL-136.

It was the second launch from that pad in a little over 32 hours, after the USSF-317 mission for the U.S. Space Force. And that quick turnaround made history.

"Massive high five to the @SpaceX west coast team for a world record launch to launch turn from Pad 4e last night! 32 hr, 3 min, 21 sec! This smashed the previous record of 45 hrs from Pad 40. Team got there with several hours of margin. Next goal… the 24 hr turn!" Kiko Dontchev, SpaceX's vice president of launch, said via X on Sunday. (Pad 40 is at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida.)

NROL-136 was the sixth launch of 2026 so far for the NRO. All of them have been carried out by SpaceX's workhorse Falcon 9, and all have delivered classified satellites to low Earth orbit.

The launch marked another step in the NRO's effort to expand its intelligence-gathering capabilities through a proliferated network of spacecraft designed to provide more frequent and timely surveillance of locations around the globe.

About two minutes after liftoff, the Falcon 9's first-stage booster separated from the rocket's upper stage, which continued carrying the classified payloads onward to orbit. The booster then reversed course and returned to Vandenberg, touching down at Landing Zone 4 approximately seven and a half minutes after launch.

Saturday's launch was the 14th flight for this particular Falcon 9 booster, dubbed B1097, which previously launched NASA's Sentinel-6B ocean-monitoring satellite, NROL-172, USSF-259 for the Space Force, and eight Starlink missions.

NROL-136 was the 15th launch dedicated to building the NRO's "proliferated architecture," the satellites for which have been developed in partnership with SpaceX and Northrop Grumman. The network is designed to increase coverage and improve the "capability and resilience" of U.S. intelligence operations in space, according to the NRO's mission website.

The NRO began deploying the constellation in May 2024 with the launch of NROL-146. The most recent proliferated architecture mission before Sunday was NROL-179, which lifted off on June 19, 2026.

As with any classified mission, the agency has not disclosed the exact number of satellites aboard NROL-136 or revealed details about their onboard technologies.

Editor's note: This story was updated at 11 p.m. ET on Nov. 22 with the news that NROL-136 set a new record for the shortest time between two launches from the same pad.

]]> <![CDATA[ This viral star projector has been hyped to Mars and back, but we hunted down the best version you can buy ]]> It was only a matter of time, but AI has come for astronomy accessories. No variant of this USB-powered star projector will break up heated dinner arguments by casting a beautifully animated space whale on the ceiling, as one ridiculous AI-generated advert asserts. Its projections are eye-catching enough to entertain space fans young and old, but they’re strictly static.

Not only are the slides smaller and blurrier than this model, a large number are dedicated to seasonal holidays. As much as I enjoy Christmas, if I had Santa’s colossal face gazing down at me from the ceiling I’d never sleep again.

More than meets the eye

I tempered my expectations when I first got my hands on the Galaxy Projector Night Light. Packed in a small, relatively unassuming box, it looks remarkably similar to the standard model that’s spread across TikTok, YouTube, Facebook and so on. Just like that one, it’s powered via USB, with a flexible stalk, a slot for slides and a nose-mounted focus wheel.

However, once I hooked it up to a handy USB socket, all my reservations vanished, and I was seriously impressed by the power of this little projector. You’ll need a darkened room but the Galaxy Projector Night Light’s larger lens is a serious step-up from the run-of-the-mill version. Its images are richer and clearer than you’d expect from a projector this size, and easily capable of transforming a mid-sized ceiling or wall into a cosmic display.

This stunning James Webb Space Telescope image of the Pillars of Creation, with its vast columns of gas and dust, is a perfect example of the projections on offer. The fact the display was static didn’t diminish its wow factor, and I spent a good 15 minutes gazing at it in wonder.

The Galaxy Projector Night Light does have a four-hour shut-off in case you drift off or want to use it to lull a child to sleep (and 12 hours for its night light function). It’s easy to adjust thanks to its flexible neck, and while it never once came loose, you’ll find some USB ports have a tighter grip than others.

Slide selection

Once I set aside the images of Santa Claus (you’re staying in the box, Saint Nick), jellyfish and a T. rex, I was left with 10 astronomy-related slides. Several, such as the black hole, are artistic illustrations, while others, like the aforementioned Pillars, are actual astronomical images.

They all have their own distinct appeal. I wouldn’t, for example, describe the black hole slide as relaxing, but it’s absolutely captivating in a cosmic horror way. I’d have appreciated an auto-rotate option, but that would have added some bulk to the projector.

Switching slides is a breeze, each image mounted in its own slide holder. Oddly, a couple of mine had hair-like marks, but those disappeared when I brought the image into focus via the nose wheel.

The full 13-slide set is:

• Angel and stars (B&W)
• Black hole
• Earth and moon
• Jellyfish
• Magellanic Cloud
• Milky Way
• Moon and stars (B&W)
• Pillars of Creation
• Santa
• Solar system
• Starfield (B&W)
• T. rex
• Whale and stars (B&W)

It’s mildly disappointing that there aren’t extra slide packs out there, but the selection is ample for entertainment, relaxation and even education. What better way to spark an interest in STEM than with the wonders of space?

Portable projection

The Galaxy Projector Night Light will run off any USB port: a laptop, desktop, charger and so on. I even got it working with my TV’s USB socket, but the real bonus was realizing I could run it off the best power banks. If you’re on the move, slip the projector and slides into one pocket, a powerbank into another, and you’re good to go for hours.

Some of the best star projectors are styled so they blend in with a room, but this one is so small you can just pack it away until you need it. The projector’s marketing even advertises it for use in the car, which seems like an accident waiting to happen. Only the Blisslights Starport is smaller, but then you’re limited to laser-dot stars.

There’s no remote and no sound options, but the Galaxy Projector Night Light is so easy to use that children should be able to get to grips with it. Literally, in fact, since while the light portion warms up, it never really gets hot. Factor in its small size and pocket-friendly price, and it’s an ideal space gift or stocking stuffer for a young stargazer.

As long as you don’t buy the hype and think you’re getting something that’ll bathe a room in beautifully animated starscapes, as several Amazon purchasers did, you’ll find this Galaxy Projector Night Light is a surprisingly capable little star projector.

Are there bigger and better models out there? Yes, and we’ve rounded up the best star projectors if this one isn’t for you. But for convenience, value for money and portability, this Galaxy Projector Night Light is a great way to bring the cosmos into your home and it’s fast cemented itself as one of my favorites.

Honestly, who can forget Alice Krige's seductive Borg Queen, Marina Sirtis’ Deana Troi tipsy on tequila, Brent Spiner's Data feeling the sensation of human skin, Patrick Stewart’s Jean-Luc Picard reliving past traumas, and James Cromwell's Zephram Cochrane blasting off in the Phoenix and dancing to Roy Orbison's "Ooby Dooby"?

We caught up with Frakes for "First Contact's" 30th anniversary to hear why this "Trek" treasure holds up and warp back to Hollywood’s heyday of the '90s. Resistance is futile!

On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night.

This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites.

The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified.

Why it mattered

From its start, the Space Transportation System, better known as the space shuttle, was a compromise between meeting civilian and military needs. NASA saw the vehicle as a means of supporting science research, establishing an on-orbit economy (servicing commercial satellites and flying company payloads) and ultimately, assembling the parts for a space station.

The Department of Defense saw the shuttle as an asset to deploying and retrieving reconnaissance satellites, among other projects, some of them classified. It was not until the loss of the space shuttle Challenger, that it was decided that the shuttle would only be used by the military when it was key to national security. Other needs would be met by expendable launch vehicles (ELVs).

As an aside, the STS-33 astronauts also spent Thanksgiving in space during this mission. But the holiday was off to a crappy start when the shuttle's toilet broke first thing in the morning. After spending most of the day fixing it, they got to enjoy their Thanksgiving turkey together.

On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light. Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast.

Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io. He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years.

To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule.

Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible.

Why it mattered

Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics.

"The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

 <title>Prvorepublikové koupaliště roky chátralo, než se ho ujali liberečtí architekti. Teď za to dostali cenu</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/prvorepublikove-koupaliste-roky-chatralo-nez-se-ho-ujali-liberecti-architekti_2611231210_zko</link>
 <description>Když se architekti z libereckého ateliéru Mjölk pustili do obnovy Lesního koupaliště, nezačali jen kreslit plány. Vzali do rukou pily a vrtačky, vyráběli nábytek, otevřeli stánek s občerstvením a postupně zapojili místní komunitu. Založili spolek, který někdejší slavnou plovárnu na úpatí Jizerských hor od roku 2020 provozuje. A do dlouhodobé proměny se zapojili spolu s místní komunitou, dobrovolníky a městem.</description>

<item>
 <title>Na českobudějovickém sídlišti otevřeli Setkávárnu. Komunitní prostor obsluhují hendikepovaní</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/na-ceskobudejovickem-sidlisti-otevreli-setkavarnu-komunitni-prostor-obsluhuji_2611231145_raf</link>
 <description>Nezisková organizace Aditus Pro otevřela na českobudějovickém sídlišti Vltava kavárnu s názvem Setkávárna. Část jejích zaměstnanců tvoří lidé se zdravotním postižením, kteří mají jinak problém s pracovním začleněním. Kavárna bude sloužit také jako komunitní prostor. „Moc doufáme, že si sem lidé ze sídliště najdou cestu a že sem budou chodit rádi a často,“ říká pro Český rozhlas České Budějovice ředitel organizace Aditus Pro Jan Šesták.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/whatsapp_image_2026-_261123-065357_raf.jpeg?itok=6YyCuF34" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:50:00 +0100</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Policie navrhla obžalovat psychoterapeuta z Prahy, který měl zneužívat ženy. Hrozí mu až 10 let vězení</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/policie-navrhla-obzalovat-psychoterapeuta-z-prahy-ktery-mel-zneuzivat-zeny-hrozi_2611231149_vdv</link>
 <description>Pražští kriminalisté navrhli obžalovat 53letého psychoterapeuta, který dle nich zneužíval a znásilňoval klientky. Muž měl pracoviště na Hradčanech, kde převážně přes noc prováděl terapie. Ženám při nich údajně podával drogy a pak využil jejich bezbrannosti. Policisté ho viní ze znásilnění, sexuálního útoku, útisku a nedovolené výroby a jiného nakládání s omamnými a psychotropními látkami a s jedy. Obvinění potvrdil mluvčí policie Richard Hrdina.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/images/82099760a5509f40e876411897c249b9.jpg?itok=KNCdXDzo" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:49:00 +0100</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Muž z Valdic, který se pokusil zabít spoluvězně, dostal doživotní trest. Rozhodl o tom krajský soud</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/muz-z-valdic-ktery-se-pokusil-zabit-spoluvezne-dostal-dozivotni-trest-rozhodl-o_2611231136_zko</link>
 <description>Krajský soud v Hradci Králové odsoudil k doživotnímu trestu muže, který loni v listopadu ve Věznici Valdice na Jičínsku na cele zaútočil na spoluvězně. Napadený přežil. Soud obžalovaného potrestal za pokus o vraždu, informovali v pondělí zástupci krajského soudu. Muž, který si odpykává trest za násilné zločiny z let 2010 a 2015 v celkové délce trvání 30 let, se k činu doznal. Rozsudek zatím není pravomocný.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/profimedia-092781850_250925-132405_jho.jpg?itok=8_QYNYFp" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:36:00 +0100</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>‚Je důležité vzdát Pepíkovi čest.‘ Lošany na Kolínsku o víkendu vzpomínaly na Josefa Mašína</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/je-dulezite-vzdat-pepikovi-cest-losany-na-kolinsku-o-vikendu-vzpominaly-na_2611231120_zko</link>
 <description>Přátelé a známí odbojáře Josefa Mašína uspořádali v neděli vzpomínkovou akci v Lošanech na Kolínsku. Na setkání mluvili Mašínovi přátelé, zazněl úryvek z knihy nebo dokumentu. Mašín zemřel letos 1. listopadu ve Spojených státech amerických. Se skupinou dalších odbojářů se v 50. letech postavil proti komunistickému režimu, při jejich činech ale zemřelo několik lidí.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/profimedia-115461726_261123-072722_med.jpg?itok=eAniL1q5" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:20:00 +0100</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Pro hasiče i milovníky staré techniky. Zlaté Hory investují do opravy hasičské zbrojnice v osadě Rejvíz </title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/pro-hasice-i-milovniky-stare-techniky-zlate-hory-investuji-do-opravy-hasicske_2611231055_aha</link>
 <description>Samospráva Zlatých Hor na Jesenicku investuje do opravy hasičské zbrojnice v osadě Rejvíz. Rekonstrukce potrvá do poloviny příštího roku. Po opravě bude v budově mimo jiné expozice dobové hasičské techniky.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/images/faa4d4d489621516a6fa07066de92e7a.JPG?itok=iolrT5ah" type="image/jpeg" />

</item>
<item>
 <title>Otevírá se další část opavského obchvatu. Výrazně pomůže s dopravou i okolním obcím </title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/otevira-se-dalsi-cast-opavskeho-obchvatu-vyrazne-pomuze-s-dopravou-i-okolnim_2611231025_aha</link>
 <description>Silničáři v pondělí otevřou další část obchvatu města Opavy. I když není dlouhý, má asi dva a čtvrt kilometru, výrazně pomůže i okolním obcím. Spojí výpadovky na Olomouc a Nový Jičín. Řadu let už na to čekají obyvatelé Otic, kde se úzkými ulicemi proplétají i kamiony.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/images/2e817f2d3037d548d8ea8cd35fb30534.jpg?itok=nnuPn2aq" type="image/jpeg" />

 <description>Přes osm let studenti z Česka i ze zahraničí pracují na nejrůznějších návrzích proměny Terezína na Litoměřicku. Poslední projekty mladých krajinářů a architektů z pražské ČVUT, Technické univerzity v Liberci nebo v Drážďanech nyní mohou návštěvníci detailně prozkoumat v prostorách terezínského Infocentra a to až do neděle 29. listopadu. </description>

Práce mají několikaměsíční zpoždění a město za úpravu okolí vodního díla zaplatí bezmála 90 milionů korun. Původně radnice počítala s částkou pod 80 milionů.</description></item><item><title>Poděkování fanouškům, absolutorium hráčům. Trenér Fodrek byl po Spartě spokojený</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/906461-podekovani-fanouskum-absolutorium-hracum-trener-fodrek-byl-po-sparte-spokojeny.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/906461-podekovani-fanouskum-absolutorium-hracum-trener-fodrek-byl-po-sparte-spokojeny.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:55:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Fotbal</category><description>Ani po výhře 3:1 na Spartě u trenéra Slovanu Branislava Fodreka nebyl vidět úsměv. Z jeho slov ale plynulo, že byl hodně spokojený, hráče chválil a děkoval i početné výpravě hostujících fanoušků. Sám ale mluvil o tom, že jeho tým na podzim čekají ještě čtyři další těžké zápasy.</description></item><item><title>V Libereckém kraji nasněžilo, silničáři radí opatrnost</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906448-v-libereckem-kraji-nasnezilo-a-misty-stale-snezi-silnicari-radi-opatrnost.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906448-v-libereckem-kraji-nasnezilo-a-misty-stale-snezi-silnicari-radi-opatrnost.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:33:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>V Libereckém kraji do rána nasněžilo a místy se stále objevují sněhové přeháňky, silnice jsou s opatrností sjízdné. Hlavní tahy jsou většinou jen holé a mokré, pozor by si měli dát řidiči v horských oblastech, kde může na silnicích ležet rozbředlý sníh.</description></item><item><title>Někdo ho vyhodil jako odpad. Malé kotě Bambi zachránila z kontejneru všímavá žena</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906414-nekdo-ho-vyhodil-jako-odpad-male-kote-bambi-zachranila-z-kontejneru-vsimava-zena.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906414-nekdo-ho-vyhodil-jako-odpad-male-kote-bambi-zachranila-z-kontejneru-vsimava-zena.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 06:30:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Tiché mňoukání z téměř prázdného kontejneru zachránilo v České Lípě život malému kotěti. Na pomoc zvířeti, které tam s největší pravděpodobností někdo úmyslně odložil, zavolala kolemjdoucí žena strážníky. Kočičí holčička Bambi nyní bojuje se zdravotními potížemi v útulku.</description></item><item><title>Sparta ve výročním zápase překvapivě prohrála s Libercem 1:3</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/906433-sparta-ve-vyrocnim-zapase-prekvapive-prohrala-s-libercem-1-3.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/906433-sparta-ve-vyrocnim-zapase-prekvapive-prohrala-s-libercem-1-3.html</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 20:09:16 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Fotbal</category><description>Fotbalisté Sparty v 15. kole první ligy ve výročním zápase překvapivě prohráli doma s Libercem 1:3 a v neúplné tabulce na čtvrté příčce ztrácejí na druhý Slovan již pět bodů. Severočeši zaostávají za vedoucí Slavií o osm bodů a k dobru mají dohrávaný duel s Ostravou.</description></item><item><title>Liberec čtyřmi góly ve druhé třetině otočil duel s Mladou Boleslaví a vyhrál 5:2</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/hokej/906431-liberec-ctyrmi-goly-ve-druhe-tretine-otocil-duel-s-mladou-boleslavi-a-vyhral-5-2.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/hokej/906431-liberec-ctyrmi-goly-ve-druhe-tretine-otocil-duel-s-mladou-boleslavi-a-vyhral-5-2.html</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 19:45:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Hokej</category><description>Hokejisté Liberce porazili ve 21. kole extraligy na svém ledě Mladou Boleslav 5:2. Bruslaři si připsali pátou prohru z posledních šesti startů, přestože po první třetině vedli.</description></item><item><title>České domácnosti dluží přes 4,5 bilionu, spotřebitelský dluh roste rekordním tempem</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906313-ceske-domacnosti-dluzi-pres-4-5-bilionu-spotrebitelsky-dluh-roste-rekordnim-tempem.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906313-ceske-domacnosti-dluzi-pres-4-5-bilionu-spotrebitelsky-dluh-roste-rekordnim-tempem.html</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 15:30:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Miroslav Adamec</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Podle údajů společnosti Czech Banking Credit Bureau (CBCB) dosáhlo celkové zadlužení obyvatel České republiky evidované v Bankovním a Nebankovním registru klientských informací na konci třetího čtvrtletí 2026 výše 4,53 bilionu korun.</description></item><item><title>Nová poznávací trasa připomene příběhy šesti zajímavých míst</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/906306-nova-poznavaci-trasa-pripomene-pribehy-sesti-zajimavych-mist.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/906306-nova-poznavaci-trasa-pripomene-pribehy-sesti-zajimavych-mist.html</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 12:30:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Zuzana Pešková</dc:creator><category>Zprávy</category><description>Od kapličky přes hřbitov až k lesnímu divadlu. Nová poznávací trasa Toulky Prosečí vzešla z participativního rozpočtu Vyšperkuj Jablonec na návrh tamního osadního výboru. Stála něco málo přes 400 tisíc korun a slavnostně se otevře 6. prosince.</description></item><item><title>Odešla hokejová legenda. Liberecké Bílé Tygry opustil František Vozka</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/906402-odesla-hokejova-legenda-liberecke-bile-tygry-opustil-frantisek-vozka.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/906402-odesla-hokejova-legenda-liberecke-bile-tygry-opustil-frantisek-vozka.html</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 10:17:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Richard Beneš</dc:creator><category>Zprávy</category><description>Fanoušci libereckého hokeje truchlí. Velká osobnost libereckého hokeje zemřela ve věku 85 let po delší nemoci.</description></item><item><title>Zastupitelstvo se měsíc po volbách rozpadlo. Lidé na Semilsku půjdou znovu k urnám</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/906312-zastupitelstvo-se-mesic-po-volbach-rozpadlo-lide-na-semilsku-pujdou-znovu-k-urnam.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/906312-zastupitelstvo-se-mesic-po-volbach-rozpadlo-lide-na-semilsku-pujdou-znovu-k-urnam.html</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 09:01:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Zuzana Pešková</dc:creator><category>Zprávy</category><description>Ve Vyskři na Semilsku budou znovu volby. Tamní zastupitelstvo se rozpadlo měsíc po komunálních volbách. Stalo se tak dva dny poté, co zastupitelé zvolili nového starostu a další členy vedení obce. Do konání nových voleb povede obec správce jmenovaný ministrem vnitra.</description></item></channel></rss>
